Subject: Re: DPA + subprocessors for EU data transfers

Julie — thanks for the note and glad the demo landed.

I attached our current DPA with commercial-legal redlines that reflect the standard Redwood posture for EU data: we operate under SCCs (controller-to-processor, EU addendum) and support customer-requested encryption-at-rest and KMS options on Dedicated/Private deployments. Exhibit A (subprocessor list) is included as a CSV — it flags hosting region and whether a subprocessors handles KV cache or metadata.

High level:
- We accept SCCs for standard hosted flows; for on-prem/VPC customers we surface KMS/HSM controls and keep full isolation options.
- We can add a short clause confirming we will provide 30 days' notice before any changes to subprocessors and offer a transition plan for any objectionable additions.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura and Marcus (copied) to review the legal redlines today.
2) If Medibase has counter-redlines, we can consolidate and aim to route for DocuSign the week of Nov 10.
3) I'll open a DocuSign envelope with the final DPA + updated Exhibit A once we align.

Attachments: Medibase_DPA_Redline_v3.docx; ExhibitA_Subprocessors_20251103.csv

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 15:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + subprocessors for EU data transfers

Quick legal read — pulled a few items that Medibase legal is likely to push back on:

- Liability cap carveouts: they typically ask for a higher cap for non-monetary damages tied to data breaches. Recommend we keep current cap but offer a limited breach response credit (one month of committed spend) as a compromise.
- Data return/deletion window: their team wants 30 days after termination; we usually do 60. Recommend we offer 45 days for hosted accounts.
- SCCs: confirm that we will execute the latest EU SCCs and that those are attached as an exhibit (we should include them).

I'll mark these in the redline and return by EOD. Marcus — if you can confirm whether we can offer the 45-day deletion window for this deal, I'll put it in writing.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Medibase Legal <legal@medibase.health>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Julie Park <julie.park@medibase.health>, t.brewer@medibase.health
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 11:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + subprocessors for EU data transfers

Laura — thanks for the read. Attached is Medibase's counter-redline (highlighted) — main asks:

1) Increase liability cap for breaches involving personal data to 12 months' fees;
2) Require notification to customer within 24 hours of a confirmed incident affecting EU personal data;
3) Objection to any broad 'business continuity' fallback that dilutes SCC protections; they want explicit language that SCCs remain the primary lawful transfer mechanism and that Redwood will not transfer EU personal data outside permitted channels without prior written approval.

We also note a small discrepancy on Exhibit A: one of your subprocessors (CacheLayer Inc.) is listed as processing KV cache in Ireland — please confirm whether that is encrypted at rest and whether keys are customer-controlled.

I'm happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that helps accelerate.

— Medibase Legal
Attachment: Medibase_DPA_Counter_v2.docx

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Medibase Legal <legal@medibase.health>, Julie Park <julie.park@medibase.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + subprocessors for EU data transfers

Thanks — appreciate the clear counter-redlines. Quick operational responses:

- Liability cap: I'll confirm with finance, but we can offer a one-time increase to 12 months' fees limited to breach-of-PII claims subject to underwriting review.
- Incident notification: Redwood will commit to 'as soon as reasonably practicable' notification; we can adopt 24 hours for confirmed incidents that materially affect EU personal data (we'll carve out time to verify scope before public disclosure).
- SCCs and transfers: Confirmed — we will attach the current EU SCC addendum and state in the DPA that SCCs govern transfers; any transfer outside those mechanisms requires prior customer consent except where legally compelled.

On CacheLayer: they process KV caches in our EU-hosted cluster; data is encrypted at rest. For hosted customers we hold the encryption keys by default, but on Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS). If Medibase requires customer-controlled keys for hosted, we can evaluate as a paid add-on.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to accept/adjust the counter in the redline (I attached the Medibase doc).
2) If we land, I'll prepare a DocuSign envelope with the final DPA + Exhibit A + SCC addendum.

I'll start the DocuSign envelope the week of Nov 10 if we have alignment.

Best,
Soojin

---
